title: Density is the mass of a material for a chosen volume
summary: Density is the mass of a substance for a specific volume. A common round figure for water is 1 gram per milliliter, and the Survey says the value at 4 degrees Celsius is a tiny bit under that.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says density, in practical terms, is the mass of a substance for a specific volume, and it quotes the classroom line that density is the mass per unit volume. A common unit it names is the gram per milliliter, or the gram per cubic centimeter. The page says the exact density of water is not really 1 gram per milliliter, but a bit less, and it prints 0.9998395 grams per milliliter at 4.0 degrees Celsius. The rounded 1 is what people usually see. The long temperature table on the page is not copied. The NIST critical-density rows, in moles per liter, are a different measurement and stay on their own card.
